vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: withings-family
Version: 1.0.1

The skill bundle is designed to fetch health data from the Withings API for multiple family members. All file system operations are confined to the designated `~/.clawdbot/withings-family/` directory, and OAuth tokens are securely stored with `0o600` permissions. Network requests are exclusively directed to legitimate Withings API endpoints (`wbsapi.withings.net`, `account.withings.com`). The `SKILL.md` instructions are clear, directly related to the skill's purpose, and contain no evidence of prompt injection or malicious directives. The OAuth flow includes CSRF protection, further indicating a focus on secure implementation.

llm.summary: The skill's code, environment requirements, and runtime instructions are consistent with its stated purpose (fetching Withings data for multiple users via OAuth); there are no signs of unexpected network endpoints or unrelated credential requests.

dimensions.detail: Name/description request only python3 and Withings client credentials, which are exactly what's needed to implement OAuth and call the Withings API. The scripts operate against Withings endpoints (account.withings.com, wbsapi.withings.net) and store per-user tokens under ~/.clawdbot/withings-family — this aligns with the multi-user Withings use case.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts limit actions to: starting a local callback server for OAuth, opening Withings auth URLs, exchanging tokens, refreshing tokens, and calling Withings API endpoints for weight/body/activity/sleep. The code only reads/writes its own config dir (~/.clawdbot/withings-family) and a local .env; it does not access other system credentials or external endpoints beyond Withings. Minor issues: oauth_local module docstring mentions port 8080 while the code uses 18081; withings.py sample in the provided excerpt appears truncated in the package listing (might be an artifact of the listing).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No automated install/downloads are specified (instruction-only with included Python scripts). No remote code downloads or extracted archives are used, which minimizes install risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only two environment variables are required: WITHINGS_CLIENT_ID and WITHINGS_CLIENT_SECRET — these directly map to the OAuth client credentials needed. No unrelated secrets or multiple disparate credentials are requested. The scripts read/offer a local .env in their own directory only.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill stores per-user OAuth tokens under ~/.clawdbot/withings-family/tokens-<user>.json. oauth_local.py attempts to set file mode 600 when saving tokens; withings.py's save_tokens function does not set permissions. The skill is not forced-always and does not modify other skills or system-wide settings. Autonomous invocation (default) is allowed but not a novel risk here given the limited scope.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: it uses Withings OAuth and API calls to fetch family members' health data and stores per-user tokens under ~/.clawdbot/withings-family. Before installing: (1) verify you are happy providing a Withings client ID/secret (these are sensitive — keep them private); (2) confirm the redirect URI you register in Withings matches the skill's localhost port (SKILL.md and code use http://localhost:18081); (3) inspect the package files locally (ensure the scripts are complete and readable — the listing showed a small docstring/port mismatch and a truncated snippet in the manifest); (4) prefer running the initial OAuth in a controlled environment (local machine) so the local callback server can run and tokens are created securely; (5) note token files are stored under your home directory — oauth_local.py sets mode 600, but withings.py's saver does not, so you may want to verify permissions after first run; (6) if you stop using the skill, revoke the app in your Withings account and delete the token files. Overall the package is internally consistent and proportional to its purpose.
